solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European infiltrating drinkers' group a negative source?

indicators.note: to infiltrate a group is to get inside it, so the European letter goes within the drinkers' group

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British beer drinkers' organisation

explanation.surface: A European has wormed their way into a beer society that may be a source of bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a well-known British pressure group for traditional beer drinkers. 'Negative' points to old photographic film, not pessimism.
explanation.definitionFit: Film photography produced negatives, and the device that exposed them is where each negative comes from.

clue.text: Fear curtailed in African country? Another one

indicators.note: in places the shortened fear word inside the name of the first African country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the fear word loses its final letter

parts.note: awe is reverential fear

explanation.surface: A clipped sense of dread lurks in one African nation, then the clue asks for a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country?' is not the definition but supplies MALI; the definition is 'Another one', meaning another African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, so it is a further country on that continent.

clue.text: It could solve rush to get a sure source of synonyms?

definitions.text: It could solve rush to get a sure source of synonyms?

indicators.note: to solve is to loosen or resolve, so these letters can be untangled into a new order
the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A reference book is pictured as the remedy for anyone hurrying to find a reliable word bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives the S of 'synonyms', which joins the letters of 'rush to get a sure' in the anagram. The whole clue also describes the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, the classic reference listing words of similar meaning.

clue.text: One in form maybe in showy performance getting hold of pair of deliveries

indicators.note: getting hold of means grasping, so the performance word wraps round the delivered letters

parts.note: a stunt is a feat performed to show off

indicators.note: a pair of means the opening two letters of the word deliveries are taken

explanation.surface: A schoolchild shows off with a flashy routine that includes two balls bowled in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, so one in a form is a pupil. 'Deliveries' sounds like cricket bowling but just gives DE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a form is a class or year group, and a pupil in one is a learner.

clue.text: Constable in van restricting parking making one-sided argument

parts.note: a special constable is a volunteer British police officer, called a special for short
P is the usual abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
to be in the van is to be at the front, so van suggests leading

explanation.surface: A police officer in a vehicle blocks a parking space while arguing only their own side.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'special' is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain. 'Van' is the vanguard, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Special pleading is a debating fallacy: citing only points favourable to oneself while ignoring the rest.

clue.text: Characteristic found in foreign money put into difficulties

indicators.note: found in means located within, so the feature word sits inside the currency word

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: Some quirk of an overseas currency leaves a person short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to restrict or constrain, especially financially, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: Steps made by supporter before game to retain on reflection basic material?

indicators.note: before puts the supporter ahead of the game
to retain is to keep hold of, so the fan-and-game pair holds the genetic letters

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the genetic letters run backwards

parts.note: DNA is the basic genetic material of living things
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A fan reaches for a game and somehow keeps hold of the stuff of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like stairs, but here means a dance. Go is a Japanese strategy board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance, and steps is a loose term for a dance.

clue.text: Idle sort representing US university endlessly?

parts.note: the American college Yale cut short is YAL, which is the three-letter word for set down turned round, so the pieces read as an instruction

explanation.surface: A lazy student is pictured as standing for an American college that goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer after three letters and read it as an instruction; following it gives YAL, Yale without its end. 'US' marks the college as American.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer who avoids work is a lazy person, an idler, and so an idle sort.

clue.text: Course of action followed by a new Asian

parts.note: a path is a course of action, the way one goes

explanation.surface: A chosen route is then taken by a newcomer from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pathan is a Pashtun, one of the people of Afghanistan and north-west Pakistan.

clue.text: Exercise taking place in museum

indicators.note: taking place in means occurring within, so the letters are found inside the word museum

explanation.surface: Some activity is going on inside a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to employ it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Advance good Greek character, academic authority

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
the head is the head teacher, the authority in a school

explanation.surface: A worthy Greek scholar is promoted to run an academic department.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ahead is to make progress or succeed, so it means to advance in life.

clue.text: Old artist getting praise in church

indicators.note: in places the praise word inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A painter of the past receives acclaim during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the established church in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Lorrain was a seventeenth-century French landscape painter, often known simply by his first name.

clue.text: Indignities a law contrived for figures in court?

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged into new words

explanation.surface: Legal humiliations are arranged for the people appearing in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but means a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are noblewomen attending a queen or princess, so they are personages at a royal court.

clue.text: Outstanding chaperone (not half)

indicators.note: not half means only half is kept, so the chaperone word loses its second half

parts.note: a duenna is an older woman chaperoning girls in a Spanish household

explanation.surface: An excellent escort is only half there.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is outstanding is unpaid and owed, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Load getting scare around back of bonfire

indicators.note: around means the fear word is placed about the bonfire's end letter

parts.note: a fright is a scare

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A heap of wood prompts alarm when it catches light behind a bonfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship, rail or truck are cargo, a load being transported.

clue.text: Island captured by unpredictable grandee won back

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the island letter sits within the rearranged nobleman
unpredictable signals that the letters of grandee come out in no fixed order

explanation.surface: An island seized by a wayward nobleman has been recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovered after losing it is the sense: something won back has been retaken.

clue.text: Joyce, perhaps, is introduced to queen in ME country

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the Middle Eastern country

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East, ME
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: Someone called Joyce meets the queen in a Middle Eastern land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joyce' is James Joyce the novelist, born in Dublin; the 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce, author of Ulysses, was born in Dublin, so he is an example of a man from Ireland.

clue.text: One backing odds regarding very good racehorse initially

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the off
on means regarding or about
so can stand for very or very good, as in the approving so-so

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of racehorse is taken

explanation.surface: A punter backs a strong-priced, excellent horse at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a backer who supports a person or event, usually with money.

clue.text: A lot of unwanted junk mail in resort

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the junk-mail word loses its last letter

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

explanation.surface: Plenty of junk messages pile up at a holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs where people go to relax, a health resort.

clue.text: A gent's drunk imbibing last of spritzer and rum

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the rearranged letters take the spritzer's last letter inside
drunk signals that the letters of a gent's are reeled into a new order
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy gentleman finishes his spritzer and rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the British adjective meaning odd. 'drunk' rearranges AGENTS, and 'imbibing' takes in R.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang rum means odd or peculiar, so it is an adjective for something weird.

clue.text: Possible summary of teetotaller's position contrary to natural inclination?

definitions.meaning: a teetotaller opposes grain spirits like whisky, so taken literally the phrase states their stance on drink
the idiom for acting in a way that goes against one's nature, from cutting wood across its fibres

explanation.surface: Someone who abstains from drink is described as behaving unnaturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something counter to one's instincts, like planing wood across its fibres.

clue.text: Dish good to move to the end for assessment

indicators.note: to move to the end means the good letter is shifted from the front to the back

parts.note: a gratin is a dish with a browned crust

explanation.surface: A good dish is reordered to get a verdict on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a score or evaluation given after judging something, so it is an appraisal.

clue.text: Popular humour by the sound of it with no purpose

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: popular is in, as in fashionable; humour is vein, a mood, as in a humorous vein

explanation.surface: Fashionable comedy is described as pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no avail is doing it fruitlessly, without any useful result.

clue.text: God taken to heart by slavish nuns

indicators.note: taken to heart means held at the centre, so the letters are found inside slavish nuns

explanation.surface: Servile nuns embrace a deity wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vishnu is one of the principal deities of Hinduism, the preserver of the universe.

clue.text: Passage around opening of drama I have abridged? It could provide colour

indicators.note: around means the passage word is put about the first letter of drama

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I have shortened is the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A passage around the opening of a play is cut short, perhaps to add colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' looks like an editing term but means I HAVE contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Food colourings are among the substances added to products, so a dye can be one.

clue.text: Single infantry soldier removing coat

indicators.note: removing its coat means stripping the outer letters off the soldier word

parts.note: grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier

explanation.surface: A lone foot soldier takes off his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' is cricket: one scored run. In cricket a single is the smallest score off a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a single is one scored point made by running between the wickets once.

clue.text: Already experienced Democrat leading island largely protected by international grouping

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the Democrat letter goes at the front
protected by means shielded inside, so the shortened island sits within the grouping

parts.note: the EU is the European Union

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the island name loses its last letter

parts.note: Java is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: A US Democrat heading for Java is sheltered by an international alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means already seen and is used for the feeling of having lived through something before.

clue.text: Fool consuming foreign bread I'd rejected — and drink!

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the fool word takes in the bread and the turned letters

parts.note: git is British slang for a foolish person
naan is a flat bread from India, also spelt nan

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters of I'd run backwards

explanation.surface: A clown eating foreign bread refuses it, then asks for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The bread and the turned letters go in after the first two letters of the fool word. The drink is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The mix is a cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth, a classic British pub drink.
